name: Psychological Report Accessibility Measure (PRAM)
description: The objective of this study is to develop the Psychological Report Accessibility Measure (PRAM), an evidence-informed tool for evaluating the accessibility of child and adolescent psychological assessment reports. Following development from an extensive synthesis of the literature, the PRAM will undergo a two-phase stakeholder evaluation process. Phase 1 will involve approximately 17 report recipients: four parents or caregivers, four teachers or education professionals, and nine young people. Participants will review the proposed domains and criteria to determine whether they reflect the characteristics that make psychological assessment reports clear, useful and accessible, and to identify any important concepts that may be missing. Because young people’s perspectives are less well represented in the existing literature, young people will also be asked additional questions about their experiences of psychological assessment reports and their preferences for how information is communicated. Their responses will be analysed separately, as well as contributing to the broader stakeholder evaluation. Feedback from Phase 1 will inform refinement of the PRAM. Phase 2 will involve eight multidisciplinary expert panel evaluating the revised instrument, including the relevance, clarity, comprehensiveness, feasibility, and usability of its domains, criteria, and scoring system as a professional report evaluation tool.
